Take a screenshot, paste it on your computer
paste-get only sees the photos you picked. Allow all photos to see new screenshots.
paste-get needs access to your photos to see new screenshots.

Copy on the phone, paste on your computer, no tap
Mode: built-in, as shell, without Shizuku. Each copy goes to your computers.
No Shizuku? paste-get can use Android\'s wireless debugging itself (experimental). It needs Developer options and Wi-Fi, and survives restarts.
In Developer options: turn on Wireless debugging, tap it, then Pair device with pairing code. Type that code in paste-get\'s notification, without leaving the code screen.
Built-in mode: waiting for Wi-Fi (wireless debugging needs it).
Tap Pair device with pairing code in Wireless debugging, then type the 6-digit code here.
Step 1 of 3: looking for the pairing code screen…
Step 3 of 3: getting permission to switch wireless debugging…
Didn\'t work: %s. Try again with a new code.
the pairing code screen wasn\'t found: keep it open while you type the code
turn on Wireless debugging in Developer options
wireless debugging didn\'t start. Is it allowed on this Wi-Fi?
wireless debugging no longer knows paste-get: pair again
Mode: Shizuku, as %s. Each copy goes to your computers.
Mode: fallback, through the system log. Each copy goes to your computers.
Mode: by hand, until the step below is done. Meanwhile, send with the Quick Settings tile or Share → Send to PC.
Android only lets the app in front read the clipboard. paste-get reads it through Shizuku, a free app that lends it the rights of the shell.
Shizuku isn\'t running. Start it again after each restart of the phone.
Shizuku is running. Allow paste-get to use it.
Shizuku can\'t watch the clipboard on this phone: %s
Shizuku stops at each restart of the phone. To go on sending copies meanwhile, paste-get needs two permissions Shizuku can grant now: reading the system log, and showing a window over other apps.
Ready for when Shizuku stops: log access and overlay allowed
For when Shizuku stops, allow paste-get to display over other apps.
Meanwhile, paste-get reads copies another way, once you open it after a restart of the phone.
Meanwhile, paste-get reads copies another way. If Android asks, allow paste-get to access the device logs.
To read each copy, a window shows for a moment, which may close the keyboard. Shizuku avoids that.
Android shows it after each copy sent. This is Android\'s own switch: it hides the notice for every app, not only paste-get. Turn it back on here or in Settings → Privacy.
Android shows \"Shell pasted from your clipboard\" after each copy sent. To hide it, turn off Show clipboard access in Settings → Privacy (it applies to every app).
Android didn\'t let paste-get change this setting: use Settings → Privacy instead
Open paste-get to send what you copy again
